# Question 1. Civil War
*Load packages and set your working directory*

*The variable `Oil` describes whether each country in the dataset is an oil exporter (Oil=1) or not (Oil=0). The variable `war` describes how many years from 1945 to 1999 that country had a civil war. # Question 3. Climate change

(a) *Begin by loading a new dataset (SeptemberTemps.csv) into R. This dataset shows the average montly temperature at NIU from 1980 to 2026. We'll focus on the month of September for the remaining questions. What is the range of the average temperature in September? What year has the highest average temperature? What year has the lowest?*


(b) *Make a scatterplot of temperature over time. Add a linear trend line. What does this suggest about how the climate is changing over time?* 

(c) *Next, subset the data into groups by decade. Start with the seventies, and then create subsets for the eighties, nineties, noughts, etc. What is the mean temperature for each decade? How is this changing over time?*

(d) *What is the standard deviation for each decade? How is the standard deviation change over time? What do the changes in standard deviation mean?*

(e) *Why is understanding changes in temperature variation, not just average temperature, important for understanding the consequences of climate change?*

*Bonus: Plot the mean and confidence interval for each decade.OR See if other months exhibit the same patterns*

# Question 5. A statistically curious friend

(a) *While at a sporting event, your statistically curious friend ask you "How does a t-test work?" Using simple language(so you can get back to the game) explain how t-tests distinguishes between two groups.*

(b) *If the result of t-test has a p-value < .05 we usually say it is statistically significant. Again, explain to your statistically curious friend what statistically significant means. Be sure to explain why .05 can be problematic?*

(c) *In statistics, we reject the null hypothesis, rather than accepting the alternative hypothesis. Explain why to your friend. Then, explain in terms of type I and type II error. *

(d) *When measuring our variables of interest we often differentiate between a conceptual definition and an operational definition. What is the difference and why is it important? Then give an example from a journal article you've read this semester.*
